Eleusis
This card game is played by four to eight players. You need two standard
decks mixed together to play this game (with no jokers, I think).
Before dealing any cards, the dealer must make up a secret rule; this is
described below. Cards are then dealt, 14 cards to each player, except
that the dealer takes no cards for himself, and does not take his own
turn in the turn order. The dealer also deals one card on the floor face
up; this starts the "main line".
The secret rule is a pure function of type ([Card] -> Card -> Bool), and
the dealer must write it down secretly in an unambiguous way; it is not
shown to the other players until the game is finished. The secret rule
depends on the cards in the main line and the card that the player is
going to play, and tells whether or not that card is valid in this case.
On each player's turn, that player can play from zero to four cards; he
must specify the order that he wishes to play them.
If he plays one card, the dealer tells him whether or not it is valid
(depending on the secret rule that the dealer defined). If it is valid,
then the card is added to the main line. If not valid, it is discarded
(and should be placed to the side of the main line to make it clear when
an incorrect card was attempted), and the player who played the wrong
card must draw two cards.
If he plays more than one card, he specifies the order and the dealer
tells him if it is valid, meaning valid to play those four in sequence.

Jacobs, sold metal cards for $1 that would allow descendants of contributors to attend the crypt's opening in 8113.

Budge in his "Egyptian Magic", however, states that it is possible that

preparation of the black ore', or `powder', which was regarded as the
active principle in the transmutation of metals.  To this name the Arabs
affixed the article `al', thus giving al-khemeia, or alchemy.

During the early centuries of Christianity, one of the
strongest threats to the development of the new religion was a 
parallel philosophical-religious movement called Gnosticism. The term 
is derived from the Greek work gnostikos, meaning "one who knows," in 
turn based on a word for "knowledge," gnosis. To the Gnostics there 
were different types of knowledge. The knowledge they claimed to have 
was not derived from ordinary sources; it was a special knowledge that 
came only from a divine revelation. It came only to a select number of 
people, and Jesus Christ was the main source of revelation.
Gnosticism is a diverse set of ideas and doctrines that became quite 
popular throughout the Mediterranean world during the 2nd and 3rd 
centuries AD. Despite some wide divergence among the many schools, the 
core belief is that there is in mankind a divine spark that can be 
awakened by its divine counterpart through the means of revelation.

or

cd directoryname		- Changes the current directory
get filename			- Gets a file
get filename local-filename	- Gets a file and changes it's name
get 00README /dev/tty		- Types this file on terminal in UNIX systems
mget *.ps.Z			- Gets multiple files. Try 'prompt' before this
quit				- Ends the FTP session
